{"type":"output_text","text":{"value":"If you're using **graphql-java** and want to enable "strict" validation or behavior when wiring your GraphQL schema using `RuntimeWiring.Builder`, you may be looking for settings or validations that enforce stricter schema definitions, such as requiring all types and resolvers to be present, or catching typo mistakes at build time.

Here's what you need to know:

---

## Does `RuntimeWiring.Builder` have a "strict" mode?

As of now, **`graphql-java`** does **not** have a specific `"strict"` flag or mode directly available in `RuntimeWiring.Builder`. The builder is used for wiring your resolvers, scalars, directives, and data fetchers to your schema.

**Example usage:**
```java
RuntimeWiring runtimeWiring = RuntimeWiring.newRuntimeWiring()
    .type("Query", typeWiring -> typeWiring
        .dataFetcher("hello", helloDataFetcher)
    )
    .build();
```

---

## Enforcing Strictness

If you want to enforce strict schema wiring **(e.g., fail if a resolver is missing)**, here are some approaches:

### 1. **Schema Validation**
After building your schema, you can use `SchemaGenerator.Options` to enable some validation on missing type resolvers:
```java
SchemaGenerator.Options options = SchemaGenerator.Options.defaultOptions()
    .enforceSchemaDirectives(true);
```
But this affects directives, not all strictness.

### 2. **Custom Schema Checks**
You can **manually validate** that every field has a data fetcher or resolver connected after building the schema. GraphQL-Java will by default fallback to `PropertyDataFetcher` if none is provided, but it won't error unless the field doesn't exist on the POJO.

### 3. **Fail Fast on Missing Bindings (Indirect)**
Some frameworks built *on top of* `graphql-java`, like **SPQR** or **GraphQL Kotlin**, optionally provide stricter schema enforcement modes.

---

## Summary

- **No explicit "strict" mode** in `graphql-java` **`RuntimeWiring.Builder`**.
- To be strict about wiring, **double-check your schema & wiring manually**, or use schema tools that offer more strictness.
- Always enable detailed logging during tests, which can help discover missing data fetchers or schema mismatches early.

             <groupId>com.azure</groupId>
             <artifactId>azure-core</artifactId>
             <version>1.55.3</version>
         </dependency>
         <dependency>
             <groupId>com.azure</groupId>
             <artifactId>azure-messaging-servicebus</artifactId>
             <version>7.17.10</version>
         </dependency>
         <dependency>
             <groupId>com.azure</groupId>
             <artifactId>azure-identity</artifactId>
             <version>1.15.4</version>
             <scope>compile</scope>
         </dependency>
         <dependency>
             <groupId>ch.poole</groupId>
             <artifactId>OpeningHoursParser</artifactId>
             <version>0.28.2</version>
         </dependency>
 
         <!-- create zip test files-->
         <dependency>
             <groupId>org.apache.commons</groupId>
             <artifactId>commons-compress</artifactId>
             <version>1.27.1</version>
             <scope>test</scope>
         </dependency>
     </dependencies>
 
     <build>
         <!--
         Filtering will perform substitution on otp-project-info.properties,
         see git commit id plugin below.
         -->
         <resources>
             <resource>
                 <directory>src/main/resources</directory>
                 <filtering>true</filtering>
             </resource>
             <resource>
                 <directory>src/ext/resources</directory>
                 <filtering>true</filtering>
             </resource>
             <resource>
                 <directory>src/client</directory>
                 <targetPath>client</targetPath>
                 <filtering>false</filtering>
             </resource>
         </resources>
         <testResources>
             <testResource>
                 <directory>src/test/resources</directory>
             </testResource>
             <testResource>
                 <directory>src/ext-test/resources</directory>
             </testResource>
         </testResources>
         <plugins>
             <plugin>
                 <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                 <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                 <configuration>
                     <annotationProcessorPaths>
                         <path>
                             <groupId>com.google.dagger</groupId>
                             <artifactId>dagger-compiler</artifactId>
                             <version>${google.dagger.version}</version>
                         </path>
                     </annotationProcessorPaths>
                 </configuration>
             </plugin>
             <plugin>
                 <groupId>org.codehaus.mojo</groupId>
                 <artifactId>build-helper-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                 <version>3.6.0</version>
                 <executions>
                     <execution>
                         <id>build-helper-generate-sources</id>
                         <phase>generate-sources</phase>
                         <goals>
                             <goal>add-source</goal>
                         </goals>
                         <configuration>
                             <sources>
                                 <source>src/main/java</source>
                                 <source>src/ext/java</source>
                             </sources>
                         </configuration>
                     </execution>
                     <execution>
                         <id>build-helper-generate-test-sources</id>
                         <phase>generate-test-sources</phase>
                         <goals>
                             <goal>add-test-source</goal>
                         </goals>
                         <configuration>
                             <sources>
                                 <source>src/test/java</source>
                                 <source>src/ext-test/java</source>
                             </sources>
                         </configuration>
                     </execution>
                 </executions>
             </plugin>
             <plugin>
                 <groupId>com.github.bohnman</groupId>
                 <artifactId>package-info-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                 <version>1.1.0</version>
                 <configuration>
                     <!-- Couldn't get this to work for main and ext code at the same time. -->
                     <sourceDirectory>${project.basedir}/src/main/java</sourceDirectory>
                     <outputDirectory>${project.basedir}/target/generated-sources</outputDirectory>
                     <packages>
                         <package>
                             <pattern>**</pattern>
                             <template>${project.basedir}/src/build/templates/package-info-template.java</template>
                         </package>
                     </packages>
                 </configuration>
                 <executions>
                     <execution>
                         <goals>
                             <goal>generate</goal>
                         </goals>
                     </execution>
                 </executions>
             </plugin>
             <plugin>
                 <groupId>com.hubspot.maven.plugins</groupId>
                 <artifactId>prettier-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                 <configuration>
                     <inputGlobs>
                         <inputGlob>src/main/java/**/*.java</inputGlob>
                         <inputGlob>src/ext/java/**/*.java</inputGlob>
                         <inputGlob>src/test/java/**/*.java</inputGlob>
                         <inputGlob>src/ext-test/java/**/*.java</inputGlob>
                         <inputGlob>src/**/*.json</inputGlob>
                         <inputGlob>src/test/resources/org/opentripplanner/apis/**/*.graphql</inputGlob>
                         <!-- Ignore patterns. -->
                         <inputGlob>!src/test/resources/org/opentripplanner/apis/vectortiles/style.json</inputGlob>
                     </inputGlobs>
                 </configuration>
             </plugin>
         </plugins>
     </build>
 </project>

**Investigating Error Messages**

I'm currently focused on dissecting the output, specifically zeroing in on three identified issues. The primary concern at the moment is a `StrictModeWiringException` related to a scalar ID that's already defined. I'm reviewing the provided line numbers for deeper insight.

**Resolving Schema Definition Conflicts**

I've identified the root cause of the `StrictModeWiringException`: a duplicate scalar ID definition in the GTFS GraphQL schema. The fix involves disabling strict mode during the `RuntimeWiring` construction, as indicated by the human repair summary. I'm now implementing this change by adding `.strictMode(false)` to the builder.

**Resolving Schema Definition Conflicts**

526. "A container for both a fare product (a ticket) and its relationship to the itinerary."
527. type FareProductUse {
528.   """
529.   Represents the use of a single instance of a fare product throughout the itinerary. It can
530.   be used to cross-reference and de-duplicate fare products that are applicable for more than one
531.   leg.
532.     
533.   If you want to uniquely identify the fare product itself (not its use) use the product's `id`.
534.     
535.   ### Example: Day pass
536.     
537.   The day pass is valid for both legs in the itinerary. It is listed as the applicable `product` for each leg,
538.   and the same FareProductUse id is shown, indicating that only one pass was used/bought.
539.     
540.   **Illustration**
541.   ```yaml
542.   itinerary:
543.     leg1:
544.       fareProducts:
545.         id: "AAA" // id of a FareProductUse instance
546.         product:
547.           id: "day-pass" // product id
548.           name: "Day Pass"
549.     leg2:
550.       fareProducts:
551.         id: "AAA" // identical to leg1. the passenger needs to buy ONE pass, not two.
552.         product:
553.           id: "day-pass"  // product id
554.           name: "Day Pass"
555.   ```
556.     
557.   **It is the responsibility of the API consumers to display the day pass as a product for the
558.   entire itinerary rather than two day passes!**
559.     
560.   ### Example: Several single tickets
561.     
562.   If you have two legs and need to buy two single tickets they will appear in each leg with the
563.   same `FareProduct.id` but different `FareProductUse.id`.
564.     
565.   **Illustration**
566.   ```yaml
567.   itinerary:
568.     leg1:
569.       fareProducts:
570.         id: "AAA" // id of a FareProductUse instance, not product id
571.         product:
572.           id: "single-ticket" // product id
573.           name: "Single Ticket"
574.     leg2:
575.       fareProducts:
576.         id: "BBB" // different to leg1. the passenger needs to buy two single tickets.
577.         product:
578.           id: "single-ticket"  // product id
579.           name: "Single Ticket"
580.   ```
581.   """
582.   id: String!
583.   "The purchasable fare product"
584.   product: FareProduct
585. }

4219. """
4220. The filter definition to include or exclude parking facilities used during routing.
4221. 
4222. Logically, the filter algorithm work as follows:
4223. 
4224. - The starting point is the set of all facilities, lets call it `A`.
4225. - Then all `select` filters are applied to `A`, potentially reducing the number of facilities used.
4226.   Let's call the result of this `B`.
4227.   An empty `select` will lead to `A` being equal to `B`.
4228. - Lastly, the `not` filters are applied to `B`, reducing the set further.
4229.   Lets call this final set `C`.
4230.   An empty `not` will lead to `B` being equal to `C`.
4231. - The remaining parking facilities in `C` are used for routing.
4232. """
4233. input ParkingFilter {
4234.   """
4235.   Exclude parking facilities based on their properties.
4236.     
4237.   If empty nothing is excluded from the initial set of facilities but may be filtered down
4238.   further by the `select` filter.
4239.   """
4240.   not: [ParkingFilterOperation!]
4241.   """
4242.   Include parking facilities based on their properties.
4243.     
4244.   If empty everything is included from the initial set of facilities but may be filtered down
4245.   further by the `not` filter.
4246.   """
4247.   select: [ParkingFilterOperation!]
4248. }

 "A container for both a fare product (a ticket) and its relationship to the itinerary."
 type FareProductUse {
   """
   Represents the use of a single instance of a fare product throughout the itinerary. It can
   be used to cross-reference and de-duplicate fare products that are applicable for more than one
   leg.
     
   If you want to uniquely identify the fare product itself (not its use) use the product's `id`.
     
   ### Example: Day pass
     
   The day pass is valid for both legs in the itinerary. It is listed as the applicable `product` for each leg,
   and the same FareProductUse id is shown, indicating that only one pass was used/bought.
     
   **Illustration**
   ```yaml
   itinerary:
     leg1:
       fareProducts:
         id: "AAA" // id of a FareProductUse instance
         product:
           id: "day-pass" // product id
           name: "Day Pass"
     leg2:
       fareProducts:
         id: "AAA" // identical to leg1. the passenger needs to buy ONE pass, not two.
         product:
           id: "day-pass"  // product id
           name: "Day Pass"
   ```
     
   **It is the responsibility of the API consumers to display the day pass as a product for the
   entire itinerary rather than two day passes!**
     
   ### Example: Several single tickets
     
   If you have two legs and need to buy two single tickets they will appear in each leg with the
   same `FareProduct.id` but different `FareProductUse.id`.
     
   **Illustration**
   ```yaml
   itinerary:
     leg1:
       fareProducts:
         id: "AAA" // id of a FareProductUse instance, not product id
         product:
           id: "single-ticket" // product id
           name: "Single Ticket"
     leg2:
       fareProducts:
         id: "BBB" // different to leg1. the passenger needs to buy two single tickets.
         product:
           id: "single-ticket"  // product id
           name: "Single Ticket"
   ```

 """
 The filter definition to include or exclude parking facilities used during routing.
 
 Logically, the filter algorithm work as follows:
 
 - The starting point is the set of all facilities, lets call it `A`.
 - Then all `select` filters are applied to `A`, potentially reducing the number of facilities used.
   Let's call the result of this `B`.
   An empty `select` will lead to `A` being equal to `B`.
 - Lastly, the `not` filters are applied to `B`, reducing the set further.
   Lets call this final set `C`.
   An empty `not` will lead to `B` being equal to `C`.
 - The remaining parking facilities in `C` are used for routing.
 """

   """
   Exclude parking facilities based on their properties.
     
   If empty nothing is excluded from the initial set of facilities but may be filtered down
   further by the `select` filter.
   """
   not: [ParkingFilterOperation!]
   """
   Include parking facilities based on their properties.
     
   If empty everything is included from the initial set of facilities but may be filtered down
   further by the `not` filter.
   """
   select: [ParkingFilterOperation!]
 }

Use the `SchemaPrinter.Options` class to exclude directives:

```java
import graphql.schema.idl.SchemaPrinter;

SchemaPrinter.Options options = SchemaPrinter.Options.defaultOptions()
    .includeDirectives(false);

- `includeScalarTypes(boolean)`
- `includeSchemaDefinition(boolean)`
- `includeIntrospectionTypes(boolean)`

SchemaPrinter.Options options = SchemaPrinter.Options.defaultOptions()
    .includeDirectives(false)
    .includeScalarTypes(true)
    .includeSchemaDefinition(true);

SchemaPrinter schemaPrinter = new SchemaPrinter(options);
```

---

**Summary:**

{"type":"output_text","text":{"value":"In `graphql-java`, the `GraphQLTypeVisitor` interface is part of the type system traversal utilities, allowing you to traverse and possibly transform the GraphQL type tree. This is particularly useful for schema transformation, validation, or schema customization scenarios.

### Key Methods of `GraphQLTypeVisitor`

The methods you typically implement when using `GraphQLTypeVisitor` (since it’s an interface) are:

#### 1. `visitGraphQLArgument`
```java
TraversalControl visitGraphQLArgument(GraphQLArgument node, TraverserContext<GraphQLSchemaElement> context);
```
- Called when visiting a `GraphQLArgument`.

#### 2. `visitGraphQLFieldDefinition`
```java
TraversalControl visitGraphQLFieldDefinition(GraphQLFieldDefinition node, TraverserContext<GraphQLSchemaElement> context);
```
- Called for each `GraphQLFieldDefinition` in the schema.

#### 3. `visitGraphQLObjectType`
```java
TraversalControl visitGraphQLObjectType(GraphQLObjectType node, TraverserContext<GraphQLSchemaElement> context);
```
- Called for each `GraphQLObjectType`.

#### 4. `visitGraphQLScalarType`
```java
TraversalControl visitGraphQLScalarType(GraphQLScalarType node, TraverserContext<GraphQLSchemaElement> context);
```
- Called for each scalar type.

#### 5. `visitGraphQLInputObjectField`
```java
TraversalControl visitGraphQLInputObjectField(GraphQLInputObjectField node, TraverserContext<GraphQLSchemaElement> context);
```
- Called for input object fields.

#### 6. `visitGraphQLEnumType`
```java
TraversalControl visitGraphQLEnumType(GraphQLEnumType node, TraverserContext<GraphQLSchemaElement> context);
```
- Called for each enum type.

#### 7. `visitGraphQLInterfaceType`
```java
TraversalControl visitGraphQLInterfaceType(GraphQLInterfaceType node, TraverserContext<GraphQLSchemaElement> context);
```
- Called for interface types.

#### 8. `visitGraphQLUnionType`
```java
TraversalControl visitGraphQLUnionType(GraphQLUnionType node, TraverserContext<GraphQLSchemaElement> context);
```
- Called for union types.

#### 9. Other type visit methods
There are similar methods like:
- `visitGraphQLInputObjectType`
- `visitGraphQLList`
- `visitGraphQLNonNull`
- `visitGraphQLEnumValueDefinition`
- etc.

### Example of Implementing a Visitor

```java
public class MyTypeVisitor implements GraphQLTypeVisitor {
    @Override
    public TraversalControl visitGraphQLFieldDefinition(GraphQLFieldDefinition node, TraverserContext<GraphQLSchemaElement> context) {
        // Custom logic here
        return TraversalControl.CONTINUE;
    }
    // implement other methods as needed...
}
```

### How to Use

You use the visitor with the schema traverser:
```java
SchemaTransformer.transformSchema(schema, new MyTypeVisitor());
```

- [graphql-java Traversal Utilities](https://graphql-java.com/documentation/schema-traversal/)

{"type":"output_text","text":{"value":"Here's guidance for **graphql-java** if you want to **remove or disable** the standard directive `@defer` or the experimental option `experimental_disableErrorPropagation`:

---

### 1. **Remove or Disable the `@defer` Directive**

In recent versions, `@defer` is a built-in directive (RFC-compliant) in `graphql-java`. If you **don't want it available** in your schema, you need to:

#### A. **Disable Defer Support in Schema Generation**

By default, when using `graphql-java`'s schema generator, it can add `@defer` automatically. You can turn this off by **customizing or filtering directives** during schema build.

For example, if using `GraphQLSchema.Builder`, you can filter directives:

```java
GraphQLSchema schema = GraphQLSchema.newSchema()
    // ... your types, queries, mutation setup ...
    .clearDirectives() // removes all directives, including @defer and @stream
    .additionalDirectives(myCustomDirectives) // re-add only those you want
    .build();
```

Or, if you're programmatically constructing the schema, don't add the `StandardDirectives.deferDirective()` to your schema.

#### B. **At Execution (Disable Defer Support Feature)**

If you’re using `graphql.execution.preparsed.PreparsedDocumentProvider`, make sure the execution input doesn't allow defer. If you use libraries (like Apollo Federated Gateway, DGS, or similar), check their documentation; they often have flags or configs to enable/disable specific directives.

---

### 2. **Remove `experimental_disableErrorPropagation`**

- This flag or feature (often found in Apollo Server and sometimes graphql-java integrations) **controls error propagation on deferred or streamed results**.
- In `graphql-java`, such experimental flags are typically set via options in the execution strategies or builders.

#### Example (If Available in Your Version):

Check your server or execution config for something like:

```java
GraphQL.newGraphQL(schema)
    .deferSupport(DeferSupport.NONE) // disables defer support if supported
    // or turn off error suppression/propagation
    .build();
```

Or, depending on how you wire the server, **simply don't set** `experimental_disableErrorPropagation` or set it to `false`.

---

### 3. **Remove `@defer` from Schema Files (SDL)**

If you use SDL (Schema Definition Language), manually remove any usage of `@defer` from your schema files.

#### Example (SDL):
```graphql
type Query {
  myField: String # @defer removed
}
```

---

## **Summary**
- To entirely remove `@defer`, **do not add or explicitly remove it from the schema** as shown above.
- The `experimental_disableErrorPropagation` flag should be **unset or deactivated** if present in your setup.
- For production, make sure clients are not sending queries using `@defer`.

data.deltaContent:
**Clarifying Directive Removal**

I'm realizing that `clearDirectives()` in graphql-java 23.0 doesn't actually remove standard, built-in directives because they're hardcoded. This makes me wonder if there's an alternative method within `SchemaPrinter` or another part of the library to achieve this, given they're always present.

**Filtering Schema Directives**

I've discovered that standard directives like `@defer` are now included by default in `schema.getDirectives()` since graphql-java 23.0. This leads me to explore how to customize the directives returned by the schema or intercept `SchemaPrinter` to exclude these built-in ones.

**Wrapping Schema Transformer**

I'm considering how to intercept the `GraphQLSchema` returned by `SchemaTransformer.transformSchema`. While I can't directly modify its construction, I believe I can wrap the resulting schema with a custom delegate to filter directives as needed.

**Investigating Schema Generation**

I'm digging into how standard directives like `@defer` are added. It seems `SchemaGenerator`'s `makeExecutableSchema` is the culprit, registering them automatically. I'm trying to see if I can intercept or modify the schema *before* `SchemaTransformer` gets involved, but the test setup in `InjectCustomDocumentationTest` might limit my options.

**Modifying Schema Directives**

I'm investigating if the `GraphQLSchema` object itself can be altered to exclude built-in directives after transformation. I'm exploring whether the `SchemaTransformer` or its visitors offer a way to influence the final `GraphQLSchema`'s directive collection directly, perhaps through a custom schema subclass or by targeting schema elements.

**Intercepting Schema Creation**

I'm exploring if reflection can be leveraged to intercept `SchemaPrinter` or override standard directives. The critical point seems to be `SchemaPrinter.print(newSchema)` where `newSchema` is created after the visitor completes during `SchemaTransformer.transformSchema`. I'm investigating if the visitor can access or modify `newSchema`'s internal fields.

**Filtering Schema Directives**

I've discovered a brilliant approach: intercepting `directiveDefinitionsHolder` during schema construction. By filtering out directives like `@defer` and `@experimental_disableErrorPropagation` using reflection, I can ensure they're entirely excluded from the final schema and `SchemaPrinter` output. I'm now investigating the optimal point within the schema transformation process, specifically around `visitGraphQLObjectType` calls, to implement this.

{"type":"output_text","text":{"value":"In **graphql-java**, the standard GraphQL directives like `@defer`, `@include`, and `@skip` are generally based on the [GraphQL specification](https://spec.graphql.org/). However, not all directives are present by default in all implementations.

### `@defer` Directive in `graphql-java`

- The `@defer` directive is **not** included in the standard built-in directives of `graphql-java` up to version 22 and even in more recent versions.
- The only built-in standard directives in `graphql-java` as of now are typically: `@include`, `@skip`, `@deprecated`, `@specifiedBy`, and sometimes `@stream`.

**Location:**
- The standard directives in graphql-java can be found in the class:  
  [`graphql.introspection.Introspection.Directives`](https://javadoc.io/static/com.graphql-java/graphql-java/17.3/graphql/introspection/Introspection.Directive.html)
- You can review the [StandardDirectives.java](https://github.com/graphql-java/graphql-java/blob/master/src/main/java/graphql/schema/StandardDirectives.java) source code on GitHub.

### About `@defer` Directive

The `@defer` directive is defined in the [GraphQL Defer Stream Specification](https://github.com/graphql/graphql-spec/blob/main/rfcs/DeferStream.md), but **it is not implemented by default in graphql-java**.

#### Current Status in graphql-java

- If you want to use the `@defer` directive in graphql-java, you will need to **define and implement it yourself** (custom directive and execution logic).
- As of 2024, there is **no built-in support** for the `@defer` directive in the core library; it’s still being discussed/implemented in the broader GraphQL community.

### Summary Table

| Directive      | Standard in core?    | Location (if available)                          |
|----------------|----------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| @skip          | Yes                  | `StandardDirectives` / `Introspection.Directives`|
| @include       | Yes                  | `StandardDirectives` / `Introspection.Directives`|
| @deprecated    | Yes                  | `StandardDirectives` / `Introspection.Directives`|
| @specifiedBy   | Yes                  | `StandardDirectives` / `Introspection.Directives`|
| @defer         | **No** (as of 2024)  | — (must be custom registered)                    |

---

**References:**
- [graphql-java StandardDirectives.java (GitHub)](https://github.com/graphql-java/graphql-java/blob/master/src/main/java/graphql/schema/StandardDirectives.java)
- [Defer/Stream RFC (GraphQL)](https://github.com/graphql/graphql-spec/blob/main/rfcs/DeferStream.md)
- [Directive Documentation](https://www.graphql-java.com/documentation/v19/directives/)

If you need an example on how to **define the `@defer` directive yourself in graphql-java**, let me know!","annotations":null},"bing_searches":null,"annotations":null}
